prediction_ref.short_label: Compute-thesis IPO supply triggers measurable AI-equity crowding by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 4 prediction watches large compute-thesis capital supply clearing the market for a measurable crowding tell - an issuer pricing below range or already-public AI names drawing down as the supply lands. Today delivers the readout side rather than the issuance side. Oracle's June 11 guide to as much as $95 billion in fiscal-2027 capital expenditure, up from $55.66 billion, sank the stock about 8.9% after-hours and dragged the PHLX Semiconductor Index down 3.57% to 12,206.46, with Nvidia and Broadcom among the heaviest weights on the S&P 500 - a correlated, same-thesis drawdown across already-public AI-infrastructure names, exactly the crowding mechanism the landing names. The reaction came despite a strong Oracle print (revenue up about 21%, cloud-infrastructure revenue up 93%), and the framing crystallized as a shift from whether AI demand is real to how the buildout gets funded. The shock also transmitted into the pre-IPO channel: Anthropic's perpetual contract on Hyperliquid fell roughly 3.7% on the same-week Fable shutdown, with the company in confidential listing preparation. What is still missing for a clean hit is a primary-market print: no below-range pricing or cut on an actual compute-thesis offering today, so this is a strong secondary-market crowding signal rather than the issuance-side tell.

prediction_ref.short_label: A frontier AI lab files a public S-1 and prices its IPO by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: This June 12 prediction tracks a frontier lab moving from confidential filing to a public S-1 and a priced offering on a US exchange. Today touches the listing question from the risk side rather than advancing the filing itself. Anthropic, already in confidential listing preparation, saw its pre-IPO shares move on the Fable shutdown: with the company shut out of selling its two most capable models worldwide under a US export-control directive, its perpetual contract on Hyperliquid fell roughly 3.7% as traders reacted, reviving questions about valuation and listing timing. The episode keeps the pre-IPO standing concrete and live - the lab whose path to a public offering the prediction watches is visibly being repriced in a tradeable proxy - while introducing a fresh governance overhang on that path: a directive that can pull a generally available flagship overnight is exactly the kind of risk factor a frontier-lab S-1 would have to disclose. The gap to the marker is direction: today's news is a valuation wobble and a timing question, not a public S-1 filing or a priced offering, so it keeps the IPO storyline warm without moving the prediction toward its landing.

prediction_ref.short_label: MCP host runtimes ship sandboxed stdio tool execution as the default by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 6 prediction is that MCP host runtimes converge on sandboxed local tool execution as the shipped default. Today's OWASP State of Agentic AI Security and Governance v2.01 supplies the strongest pressure yet for that default. The report positions prompt injection as the dominant attack vector mapped to six of ten OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications categories, and its new Real-World Incidents tracker ties concrete failures directly to the MCP and tool-execution surface: the MCP RCE CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6), an OpenAI Codex CLI sandbox bypass (CVE-2025-59532), the Cursor environment-poisoning flaw CVE-2026-22708, and the March 2026 LiteLLM backdoor that shipped an autonomous attack bot in roughly 47,000 downloads over three hours. With coding agents now the center of agentic risk (28 of 53 tracked projects) and an MCP remote-code-execution CVE cataloged at the top of the severity scale, the report is precisely the kind of incident-driven evidence that forces host runtimes to treat stdio tool execution as something to isolate by default. The gap to the marker is that the report documents the threat and the CVEs rather than a host runtime actually shipping process or container isolation as the default - it is the strongest case-for-the-default rather than the default itself landing.

That incident-driven pressure is the strongest case yet for the Q2 2027 prediction's sandboxed-stdio default.
bridge.remaining_gap: The report makes the case but no host runtime actually ships process or container isolation as its stdio-execution default, which is the marker's landing condition.

prediction_ref.short_label: Durable agent-execution substrate hardens into a standard primitive by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 12 prediction tracks durable, long-horizon agent execution - cloud-sandbox or local-swarm style - hardening into a standard primitive as a third lab or harness ships it. Today supplies two adjacent reinforcements on the substrate side. Huawei rebuilt HarmonyOS 7 around an OS-level agent runtime via the new HarmonyOS Agent Framework 2.0, framing the model as Intention as Service that compresses multi-step operations into a single conversation through task decomposition, tool calling and autonomous execution, and claiming a task-execution success rate above 90% across phones, tablets, PCs, wearables and IoT - autonomous multi-step execution baked into the device platform rather than bolted on as an app. Separately, two June arXiv papers treat memory for long-running agents as an infrastructure problem: Infini Memory proposes a maintainable persistent-memory architecture (64.7% on MemoryAgentBench), and Agent Memory offers a systems characterization with a phase-aware profiling harness across ten memory systems. Both push the same instinct the prediction names - persistent, long-horizon agent execution treated as durable infrastructure. The divergence from the exact marker is that Huawei's framework is an OS-level autonomous-execution runtime rather than the specific cloud-sandbox or local-swarm durable-agent shape, and the arXiv work studies memory systems rather than shipping a durable-execution primitive, so this is substrate-trend reinforcement rather than a third clean instance.

prediction_ref.short_label: Open agent harness powers a second vendor's first-party agent by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: The June 4 prediction tracks an open agent harness becoming the substrate beneath another vendor's shipped first-party agent. Today's Huawei announcement is a concrete instance of the broader pattern: at its Developer Conference Huawei shipped a first-party agent built directly into HarmonyOS 7 through the new HarmonyOS Agent Framework 2.0, an OS-level agent architecture coordinating task decomposition, tool calling and autonomous execution across a large catalog of specialized agents, with a developer beta out now and general release this fall. That is a major platform vendor packaging a branded first-party agent on its own agent-framework substrate, which is the spirit of the prediction. The same day, Moonshot published open-weight Kimi K2.7-Code (1-trillion-parameter MoE, about 32B active, 256K context) tuned for long-horizon agentic software engineering under a Modified MIT license, extending the openly published stack that first-party agents can build on. The gap to the exact marker is that Huawei's framework is its own first-party harness rather than a separately published open agent-harness framework adopted by a second distinct vendor, and Kimi K2.7-Code is an open model rather than an adopted harness - so this is supporting evidence for first-party agents on open or self-built stacks rather than a clean second-vendor-adopts-an-open-harness hit.
